content.text:
The findings are fair. Both point at a real asymmetry I introduced. I'll make `OwnerEmail` the genuine single authority by removing the generated `@Email` constraint (so Jakarta doesn't become a competing validity definition on the update path) and routing both pipelines through `OwnerEmail` in their *validate* steps, leaving `ApplyOwner` a straight copy.

Let me check the current `ValidateOwner`:
Now remove `format: email` from the OpenAPI spec so the generated DTO no longer carries a competing `@Email` constraint:

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets
    OwnerPage:
      title: Owner page
      description: A page of pet owners.
      type: object
      properties:
        content:
          title: Content
          description: Pet owners in the requested page.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/Owner'
        page:
          title: Page
          description: Zero-based page index.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 0
        size:
          title: Size
          description: Requested page size.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 1
          example: 5
        totalElements:
          title: Total elements
          description: Total number of owners matching the request.
          type: integer
          format: int64
          minimum: 0
          example: 10
        totalPages:
          title: Total pages
          description: Total number of pages matching the request.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 2
      required:
        - content
        - page
        - size
        - totalElements
        - totalPages
    PetPage:
      title: Pet page
      description: A page of pets.
      type: object
      properties:

content.text:
The `@jakarta.validation.constraints.Email` annotation is gone — only the plain field/accessors remain. Both findings are addressed and the suite is green (`Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`).

## What I changed and why

I agreed with both findings — they describe a real asymmetry I introduced. The fix makes `OwnerEmail` the one authority and makes the two pipelines symmetric:

**Finding #1 — duplicated/divergent validity rule.** The problem was that `format: email` in the OpenAPI spec made the generated DTO carry `@jakarta.validation.constraints.Email`, so the `@Valid`-bound update path was silently validated by Jakarta while the create path used `OwnerEmail.isValid`. Rather than route both through Jakarta (impossible without `@Valid` on the create step, which would change the missing-field error shape), I made `OwnerEmail` the sole authority:
- Removed `format: email` from `openapi.yml` (kept the property and `maxLength: 255`), dropping the `@Email` constraint from the generated DTO — verified above.
- `ValidateOwner` now validates email explicitly via `OwnerEmail.isValid` and throws the same checked `InvalidEmailException` (→ `400 {"errors":["email"]}`) as the create path.

**Finding #2 — normalization in the wrong unit on the update path.** Moved `OwnerEmail.normalize(...)` out of `ApplyOwner` and into `ValidateOwner`, mirroring how `ValidateNewOwner` handles it on create. `ApplyOwner` is back to a straight field-copy (`owner.setEmail(request.getEmail())`), so it no longer looks odd next to the raw telephone copy.

Net result: both pipelines bind/validate/normalize email in their `Validate` step through `OwnerEmail`, so its "single source of truth" javadoc is now accurate (I also added a sentence to `ValidateOwner` noting why it uses `OwnerEmail` instead of an `@Email` constraint). Acceptance behaviour is unchanged: mixed-case email stored lower-cased, `not-an-email` rejected 400, missing email accepted.

One note on scope: removing `@Email` means the update path no longer *bean-validates* email, but it does validate it through `OwnerEmail` instead — equivalent coverage, now consistent. The other DTO field constraints (name/telephone patterns) are untouched and still enforced via `@Valid` on the update path.
